title: Cornbread
subtitle: Southern American skillet cornbread
excerpt: A crisp-bottomed, tender cornbread baked in a cast-iron skillet. Not sweet in the Southern style, with a golden crust and a crumbly, open crumb.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cornbread is a staple of Southern American cooking, with deep roots in Native American corn cookery. The Southern style is traditionally unsweetened, whereas Northern and Midwest versions are often sweeter. Baking in a hot cast-iron skillet produces the characteristic crisp base.

recipeTools.notes: A 25 cm cast-iron skillet gives the best crust.

content.text: Cornbread is a quick bread made with cornmeal, buttermilk, and egg, baked in a hot cast-iron skillet. The hot fat in the pan sets the base instantly, giving a crisp, almost fried crust while the inside stays tender and crumbly. It takes about 10 minutes to mix and 25 minutes to bake.
Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Place the cast-iron skillet in the oven as it heats.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, eggs, and oil. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are fine.
Carefully remove the hot skillet from the oven using oven gloves. Add the butter and swirl quickly until melted and coating the base and sides. Pour the batter in immediately.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and a skewer comes out clean. Leave to cool in the skillet for 5 minutes, then turn out. Eat warm.
